content.text: Writing both plans into `docs/`:

input.content:
# Typst-native editor — brief plan

Status: proposal. Nothing built.

## What "Typst-native" should mean

The writer keeps writing in the page-view editor they have now. What changes is the document's source of truth:
it becomes a Typst document instead of HTML, and Typst sets the pages. The writer should never have to see
markup unless they open a source view.

The default is **not** a code editor for Typst. The text-first mode is an opt-in view of the same document.

## What it touches (measured 2026-09-23)

| Area | Today | Files |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Editor schema | Tiptap/ProseMirror, 33 extensions under `src/components/editor/extensions` | 33 |
| Storage | `folio-content.html` in IDB; `html: v.string()` in `convex/schema.ts` | ~25 read/write `.html` |
| Pagination | our own measurement engine (`__twynePagination`) | 15 |
| Export | DOCX (`exchange-docx`), PDF/print, markdown | 3 + 7 + 5 |
| Publishing | `htmlToMarkdown`/`stripHtml` → standard.site, micropub, blog | 5 |
| AI | prompts, personas, editorial notes all read manuscript HTML/text | many — read-only |

Rewriting the editor would touch most of the app. A bridge does not have to.

## Recommended shape: bridge, don't replace

1. **ProseMirror ↔ Typst serializer (both directions)** for the schema we already have: paragraphs, headings,
   marks, lists, quotes, notes, drop cap, and page layout settings. HTML stays the storage format in phase 1.
2. **Typst as the typesetter.** Compile with the typst WASM build (typst.ts) in a worker.
   - Use it for PDF export and a "proof" pane first.
   - Our measurement pagination stays for live editing until the proof matches it.
3. **Source view.** A CodeMirror pane with the Typst source of the current folio. Edits round-trip through the
   serializer. Anything the serializer can't represent is kept as an opaque "raw Typst" node, so it is never
   lost.
4. **Flip the source of truth** (only if 1–3 prove out).
   - Store `.typ` alongside HTML; add a `format` field to folio content and to the Convex schema.
   - Migrate lazily when a folio is opened.
   - Publishing and AI keep reading derived HTML/markdown.
5. **Retire the measurement pagination** once Typst proof and live view agree on page breaks.

## Risks

- WASM bundle size (typst.ts is several MB). Lazy-load it, and ship it inside the desktop app.
- Fonts: Typst needs the actual font files. We already commit Libre Baskerville cuts for OG cards, so reuse them.
- Round-trip fidelity. Collaborative edits and AI suggestions operate on ProseMirror steps. Typst is the output,
  not the editing model, until phase 4.
- Two paginators disagreeing during the transition. Label the Typst one "proof".

## First slice (about a week)

Serializer for the current schema + a "Export → PDF (Typst)" menu item + round-trip unit tests on the e2e
fixtures. That shows whether fidelity is achievable before anything else commits.

# Local & shipped models — brief plan

Status: proposal. Measurements come from Keating's on-device ledger
(`~/Projects/keating/scripts/on-device-site`).

## Models

| Model | Size | Where it runs | Job |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `minishlab/potion-retrieval-32M` (ONNX) | ~131 MB, 512-d, ~4 ms/batch in Keating | **Desktop (bundled)** | Retrieval over folios, notes, apparatus, references |
| `minishlab/potion-multilingual-128m-onnx` | ~547 MB (model 512 MB + 35 MB tokenizer) | **Convex / server, on request**; optional desktop download | Multilingual retrieval, matching the multilingual replies |
| KEV-0.8B (the local Jev) | 0.8B params | **Desktop (bundled or first-run download)** via the existing `desktop/litert-server.ts` | Offline editorial review / notes |

Static (potion) embeddings are a lookup plus a mean, with no transformer at inference time. That is why the 32M
model is cheap enough to ship. The multilingual model is too heavy for the browser, which is why the web
calls the server for it.

## Routing

- **Desktop:** potion-32M and KEV run locally. The multilingual model is used when installed, otherwise the
  server.
- **Browser:** embeddings come from the server (multilingual). Twyne does not download 500 MB into a tab.
- **Server:** multilingual embedding as an action. Convex actions have runtime/memory limits, so it likely needs a
  small sidecar (the Railway service) that Convex calls. Verify before committing to an in-Convex ONNX runtime.
  Store vectors with a Convex `vectorIndex`.
- Keep one `EmbeddingProvider` interface (`embed(texts) → Float32Array[]`, `dimensions`, `modelId`).
  - Never mix vectors from different models in one index.
  - Key the index by `modelId`.

## Offline is degraded — say so

- Add a single "Offline mode" notice in settings and in the editor status area. It lists what changes:
  - KEV notes are shorter and less reliable than hosted Jev.
  - Search is literal-strong but weaker on paraphrase. Keating: potion-32M paraphrase MRR ≈ 0.55 vs literal 1.0.
  - Research/web features are unavailable.
- Tag every output that came from a local model, so a writer can tell offline quality apart from hosted quality.

## Paid trained models (separate from Pro)

`docs/pricing-rollout.md` already keeps custom training out of `twyne_pro_v2`, so this is a separate product:

- **Fine-tuned potion** distilled on the writer's own corpus: better paraphrase search on their material.
- **Fine-tuned KEV** on house style / editorial rubric: offline notes that sound like their editor.
- Billed per training run plus delivery. Delivery means a downloadable desktop model, or hosted.

## Waitlist + survey

- A waitlist form on the pricing page ("Trained models — join the waitlist") that stores email, plan, and one
  optional line about what they write.
  - Use a Convex table `waitlist` with the fields: `email`, `userId?`, `source`, `createdAt`, `surveySentAt?`.
- Later: send a short survey (corpus size, languages, desktop vs hosted, price anchor) to the list in one batch.
  Record `surveySentAt` so nobody is asked twice.
- Gate the form behind a feature flag, like the other pricing gates.

## Order

1. `EmbeddingProvider` + potion-32M in desktop + offline notice.
2. Server multilingual endpoint + vector index.
3. Ship KEV through `litert-server`.
4. Waitlist table + form. The survey is sent when there is something to price.

- **Server:** multilingual embedding as an action. Convex actions have runtime/memory limits, so it likely needs a
  small sidecar (the Railway service) that Convex calls. Verify before committing to an in-Convex ONNX runtime.
  Store vectors with a Convex `vectorIndex`.
- Keep one `EmbeddingProvider` interface (`embed(texts) → Float32Array[]`, `dimensions`, `modelId`).
  - Never mix vectors from different models in one index.
  - Key the index by `modelId`.

## Offline is degraded — say so

- Add a single "Offline mode" notice in settings and in the editor status area. It lists what changes:
  - KEV notes are shorter and less reliable than hosted Jev.
  - Search is literal-strong but weaker on paraphrase. Keating: potion-32M paraphrase MRR ≈ 0.55 vs literal 1.0.
  - Research/web features are unavailable.
- Tag every output that came from a local model, so a writer can tell offline quality apart from hosted quality.

## Paid trained models (separate from Pro)

`docs/pricing-rollout.md` already keeps custom training out of `twyne_pro_v2`, so this is a separate product:

- **Fine-tuned potion** distilled on the writer's own corpus: better paraphrase search on their material.
- **Fine-tuned KEV** on house style / editorial rubric: offline notes that sound like their editor.
- Billed per training run plus delivery. Delivery means a downloadable desktop model, or hosted.

## Waitlist + survey

- A waitlist form on the pricing page ("Trained models — join the waitlist") that stores email, plan, and one
  optional line about what they write.
  - Use a Convex table `waitlist` with the fields: `email`, `userId?`, `source`, `createdAt`, `surveySentAt?`.
- Later: send a short survey (corpus size, languages, desktop vs hosted, price anchor) to the list in one batch.
  Record `surveySentAt` so nobody is asked twice.
- Gate the form behind a feature flag, like the other pricing gates.

## Order

1. `EmbeddingProvider` + potion-32M in desktop + offline notice.
2. Server multilingual endpoint + vector index.
3. Ship KEV through `litert-server`.
4. Waitlist table + form. The survey is sent when there is something to price.

Ctrl+A is fixed. The notorganic PDS is up and Twyne's publish code matches what's already on it, but the actual post needs you to sign in. I've also written the two plans you asked for.

**Ctrl+A.** The handler only listened on the text area, so it only worked when the cursor was already in the text. After you clicked a toolbar button like Bold, Ctrl+A selected nothing. It now works from anywhere in the editor: the whole manuscript is selected and the cursor goes back into it. Text fields and dialogs keep their normal select-all.
- New test file `e2e/select-all.e2e.ts` covers five cases in both paginated and continuous layout. All 10 runs pass. The toolbar case failed before the fix.
- 4 tests in `formatting.e2e.ts` time out waiting for a "Type options" button. They fail the same way on the version before my change, so this fix didn't cause it.
- The fix is in `src/components/editor/twyne-editor.tsx`.

**Publishing a standard.site post to the notorganic PDS**
- `pds.notorganic.info` is live and handles its own sign-in.
- It holds four accounts: `keatingjev`, `stich-agent`, `keating-pilot-f0b4`, and `blog.keating.help`. I couldn't tell which one you mean.
- `blog.keating.help` already has standard.site records. Twyne's publication and document records match their format, so posts should be readable by the same tools.
- **I can't sign in for you.** Entering account passwords is off-limits for me, and the browser extension isn't connected anyway. To publish:
  1. Open a folio on twyne.love.
  2. Folio menu → Share → sign in with the handle, e.g. `keatingjev.pds.notorganic.info`.
  3. Choose publish to PDS. Twyne creates the publication record, then the document.
- One risk: Twyne asks for a newer bundled permission (`include:site.standard.authFull`) that this PDS doesn't list as supported. If sign-in fails with a scope error, falling back to the standard `atproto transition:generic` scope for PDSes that don't support it is a small change.
- Tell me which account and I'll confirm the post landed and check the record once you've published.

**Typst-native editor:** `docs/typst-native-editor-plan.md`. A full rewrite would touch most of the app: 33 editor extensions, about 25 files that read or write HTML, 15 for pagination, plus export and publishing. So the plan builds a two-way converter and uses Typst first for PDF export and a proof view. Switching the saved format to Typst comes only after that proves out. The first slice is a Typst PDF export plus tests that convert documents to Typst and back, about a week.

**Models, paid training, and waitlist:** `docs/local-models-plan.md`.
- **Desktop:** potion-retrieval-32M (about 131 MB) and KEV-0.8B ship with the app.
- **Browser:** the server runs potion-multilingual, which is about 547 MB, too big for a browser tab.

# Not Organic signup deployment — 2026-09-06

The PDS, portal server, and public identity frontend deployed successfully:

| Service | Deployment |
| --- | --- |
| PDS | `593e565a-0bb0-4f4d-be2a-079196becef9` |
| Portal | `7ee71b97-f12c-4758-ba3e-67dd34d084ef` |
| Landing / identity frontend | `47907b76-0168-45bf-aaa9-0dea0d6b4dad` |

PDS signing and admin secrets were generated directly into Railway and existing
secrets were preserved. Registration is configured without invites, with handles
under `.pds.notorganic.info`. The existing `/pds` persistent volume is retained.

Private bucket `notorganic-pds` in Railway's `iad` region supplies blob storage
and account-database backups. Credentials are server-held. An empty disposable
object passed PUT/GET/DELETE (200/200/204), and Litestream logged its first
account-database snapshot upload. This does not prove a full disaster recovery
of every PDS database and actor repository. The old R2 endpoint failed TLS;
its credential values were not printed or copied into source.

The public identity frontend serves the Create account action. Session checks
return 401 when signed out, and OAuth metadata and public JWKS return 200.
The initial signup check returned the expected 503 before PDS DNS was
configured. No real account creation or SMTP delivery is claimed.

## DNS configuration

These records were added to Porkbun using Sesame with credentials loaded
directly from Skate. Existing unrelated DNS records were preserved:

| Type | Host | Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CNAME | `pds` | `4uty3sp7.up.railway.app` |
| CNAME | `*.pds` | `otyc38dm.up.railway.app` |
| CNAME | `_acme-challenge.pds` | `otyc38dm.authorize.railwaydns.net` |
| TXT | `_railway-verify.pds` | `railway-verify=db82d27f50380b411870e94b3d2145420605c2a4038c78861f81add31f315451` |

The TXT value is a public domain-ownership verification token. Recheck required
values with `railway domain status` before changing records if a domain has
since been removed or recreated. Railway confirmed the CNAME records had
propagated, and Google's public resolver returned the ownership TXT record.
Certificate issuance was still pending at that check.

## Remaining email and end-to-end verification

Use **Resend** for SMTP, as requested. Set `PDS_EMAIL_SMTP_URL` to a secure SMTP
URL using `smtp.resend.com:465`, username `resend`, and the URL-encoded Resend
API key as its password. Set `PDS_EMAIL_FROM_ADDRESS` to an address on a domain
verified in Resend. Do not put SMTP passwords in chat or source control.
Redeploy the existing PDS image after changing these settings, preserving the
volume and generated identity keys.

An internal Railway SSH check returned 200 for PDS health (version 0.4.219),
server description (`inviteCodeRequired: false`, domain `.pds.notorganic.info`),
and OAuth metadata (issuer `https://pds.notorganic.info`). These checks do not
substitute for public DNS/TLS and a completed registration.

Then follow the account signup verification steps in `infra/runbook.md`, using
a fresh browser session and a controlled test email address. Porkbun access was
subsequently recovered through Skate; no Resend key was found in Skate, and the
configured OpenBao credential cannot list secret metadata. An authenticated
browser was unavailable, so no browser signup was performed. The external Vet
review remains unapproved and was not retried.

4. Copy the record URI, open its reading view, or inspect the ATProto record.

Twyne creates or reuses a `site.standard.publication` record and files the
folio as a `site.standard.document` with its Markdown content. **Re-publish
(update)** updates the same PDS document record; **Unpublish from PDS** deletes
that document from your PDS. Twyne keeps the record key locally only so it can
update or remove the correct record later.

## 3. Publish to an existing Micropub site

Use this only if you already operate a site with a Micropub endpoint.

1. Open **File** > **Share** and find the Micropub section.
2. Enter your HTTPS Micropub endpoint and an access token.
3. Publish the folio.

Twyne sends the title and article HTML to that endpoint as a published
Micropub entry. The access token is used for that request and is not retained
by Twyne.

## Relationship to Keating

Twyne's PDS publishing uses the same Standard.site document format that
Keating reads, but it creates or reuses the writer's _Twyne_ publication. It
does not automatically add a post to Keating's configured publication. To put
the same work in Keating, create or update a `site.standard.document` in the
ATProto repository configured for Keating, point its `site` field at Keating's
`site.standard.publication` record, and use a path such as `/blog/my-post`.
See the Keating guide for the one-time publication setup and its environment
configuration.

The **Your own repo** section is at the bottom of the Share dialog. Without an
ATProto session it shows only "Connect Bluesky…" and no publish button, so
sign in first.

### Using a Not Organic PDS account

Not Organic accounts live on `https://pds.notorganic.info`, with handles such
as `yourname.pds.notorganic.info`. Any of these handles works in step 1:

1. Open the editor's office (top right) → **Bluesky or PDS identity**.
2. Enter the handle, e.g. `yourname.pds.notorganic.info`. You can also enter
   the PDS URL `https://pds.notorganic.info`.
3. Approve on the PDS's own sign-in page. Twyne never sees the password.
4. Return to the folio → **File** → **Share** → **Publish to your PDS**.

Known limitation: Twyne requests the `include:site.standard.authFull`
permission set. As of 2026-09-23, `pds.notorganic.info` (PDS 0.4.219) lists
only `atproto` and the `transition:*` scopes. If approval fails with a scope
error, the fix is for Twyne to fall back to `atproto transition:generic` on
servers that don't list permission sets.

To check a publish independently, list the document records in your repo:

```sh
curl "https://pds.notorganic.info/xrpc/com.atproto.repo.listRecords?repo=<your-handle>&collection=site.standard.document"
```

# Not Organic–native sign-in and data — inventory and plan

Status: inventory done 2026-09-23. The migration has not started.

The goal is to make Twyne work the way Keating does:
- one Not Organic account (a DID, usually on `pds.notorganic.info`) is the writer's identity;
- wallet, inference, publishing and synced data all hang off that account.

## 1. How sign-in works today

Twyne has **three independent identity systems**:

| # | Path | Where | What it creates |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | **better-auth**: email OTP (Resend) + passkeys | `convex/auth.ts`, `convex/auth.config.ts`, `src/utils/auth-client.ts`, `src/components/auth/auth-panel.tsx` | The Convex user. **All server data** (folios sync, comments, published pieces, profiles, subscriptions) is keyed to it. |
| B | **Bluesky / ATProto OAuth** | `src/utils/atproto.ts`, `/oauth-client-metadata.json`, `auth-panel.tsx` "Bluesky or PDS identity" | A *browser-only* session, `auth.value.provider === "atproto"`. No Convex user, so Twyne-hosted publish is unavailable. Used for PDS publishing. |
| C | **Not Organic link** (PKCE, `wallet:read`) | `src/utils/notorganic-connect.ts`, `src/components/settings/notorganic-connection.tsx`, `convex/providerIdentity.ts`, `convex/lib/notorganic.ts`, `convex/lib/providerLink.ts` | Not a sign-in. It **links** a DID to an existing better-auth user (`saveVerifiedLink`). Server then signs product assertions → `/v1/auth/token/exchange` for wallet and inference. |

`src/utils/auth-context.tsx` switches between `provider: "convex"` (A) and `provider: "atproto"` (B).
`linkDidFromLegacyBrowserSession` is the bridge from an old B session to a DID link.

## 2. How Keating does it (target)

- **Sign-in:** `id.notorganic.info/authorize` with PKCE → `POST api.notorganic.info/v1/public/token`.
  - The response is a 300-second DPoP-bound capability whose `sub` is the account DID.
  - `device_session: true` adds a rotating refresh token (`/v1/public/device/token`, revoke via
    `/v1/public/device/revoke`).
  - The DPoP key is a non-extractable WebCrypto key.
- **Identity:** `GET /v1/account` (any scope) with the capability.
- **Data:** local-first.
  - Encrypted sync; the key comes from `GET /v1/sync/account-key` (scope `sync:key:read`).
  - Transport is Gun P2P.
  - No Keating-owned user table.
- **Publishing:** the same DID's repo on the PDS (standard.site).
- `https://twyne.love` is **already an approved public client** for product `twyne` in the gateway
  (`apps/gateway/src/public-client-product.ts`).

## 3. Creem (payments) — where it still is

New sales already go through Not Organic (`createNotOrganicCheckout` in `src/routes/pricing/index.tsx`,
credit packs in `convex/lib/providerCheckout.ts`). Creem remains **only for legacy subscribers**:

| Kind | Files |
| --- | --- |
| Live server path | `convex/http.ts` (webhook), `convex/payments.ts` (`createCheckout` — no UI caller left; `getMySubscription`, `applyCreemEvent`), `convex/lib/creem.ts`, `convex/lib/entitlement.ts` (`CREEM_PRO_PRODUCT_IDS`), `convex/schema.ts` (subscriptions table), `convex/profiles.ts`, `convex/lib/rateLimit.ts` |
| UI | `src/routes/pricing/index.tsx` reads `api.payments.getMySubscription`; `src/utils/subscription-plan.ts` comment |
| Config | `.env.example` (12 lines), `package.json` `test:creem*`, `playwright.config.ts` |
| Tests/scripts | `tests/creem.test.ts`, `tests/entitlement.test.ts`, `scripts/creem-smoke.ts`, `scripts/setup-creem-e2e.ts`, `e2e/journey.e2e.ts`, `e2e/collaboration.e2e.ts` |
| Docs | `docs/architecture/data-and-sync.md`, `docs/my-desk-usage-profile-spec.md` |

**Safe to remove now:**
- `payments.createCheckout` and its rate-limit bucket;
- the Creem checkout e2e setup.

**Keep until the last legacy subscription ends:**
- the webhook;
- the subscriptions table;
- the entitlement lookup.

## 4. Plan

Convex stays the data store. Its customJwt verifier doesn't cover the gateway's EdDSA, DPoP-bound tokens, so
Not Organic is bridged into better-auth rather than replacing it.

1. **Not Organic as the sign-in** (single button: "Continue with Not Organic").
   - Browser PKCE + DPoP against `id.notorganic.info`, with `device_session: true`.
     Reuse `notorganic-connect.ts` and the Keating `oauth.ts` flow.
   - Browser sends `{access_token, dpop_proof for GET /v1/account}` to a new better-auth endpoint
     (`/api/auth/sign-in/notorganic`).
   - That endpoint calls `/v1/account`, gets the DID, and finds or creates the user through the existing
     `providerIdentity` DID link. It then issues the normal better-auth session, so every Convex query keeps
     working unchanged.
   - Scopes: `wallet:read infer:* sync:key:read`, requested once.
2. **Existing accounts.**
   - Email/passkey users sign in the old way once. The existing link flow attaches their DID, and after that
     Not Organic is their sign-in.
   - Keep email OTP as a hidden "recover old account" path until linked accounts dominate.
3. **Collapse ATProto into the same identity.** The DID from step 1 *is* the writer's PDS repo, so:
   - PDS publishing uses that account;
   - it requests ATProto OAuth against its PDS only when writing records;
   - the separate "Bluesky session" mode and the `provider: "atproto"` split in `auth-context.tsx` go away.
   - Third-party Bluesky PDS accounts remain a "publish elsewhere" option, not an identity.
4. **Data, native like Keating.**
   - Local-first IDB stays primary; Convex sync is keyed by DID-linked user.
   - Optional later: encrypt synced folio content with the `/v1/sync/account-key` key, so the server holds
     ciphertext, as in Keating.
5. **Creem retirement.** Remove `createCheckout` now; the webhook and table stay until the last legacy
   subscription lapses.

## Risks / open questions

- The gateway must allow CORS from `https://twyne.love` for `/v1/public/token` and `/v1/account`.
  - `twyne.love` is registered as a client; CORS is not verified yet.
  - Desktop needs a loopback callback, like Keating's `CORS_ALLOW_LOOPBACK`.
- The capability lives 300 s. Server-side work (wallet, inference) keeps using the existing product-assertion
  exchange rather than the browser token.
- Existing users with Creem subscriptions must keep their entitlement after switching to a Not Organic sign-in.
  - Entitlement follows the Convex user, and step 2 keeps the same user, so this holds only if the linking
    happens *before* the first Not Organic-only sign-in.

# Publishing from Twyne

Twyne offers three separate ways to make a folio public. Choose the one that
matches where you want the finished piece to live.

## 1. Publish on Twyne

Use this for the quickest public link hosted by Twyne.

1. Open the folio you want to publish.
2. Open the **File** menu in the editor toolbar, then open **Share**.
3. Press **Publish now**.
4. Copy the resulting link or open the public reading view.

Anyone with that link can read the piece but cannot edit it. Press
**Unpublish** in the same panel to take the Twyne-hosted page down. This option
requires a Twyne email or passkey account; it is not available in a Bluesky
session. A regular writer publishes a shareable post under their claimed
writer handle. A Twyne blog administrator publishes to the main `/blog` feed;
non-administrators cannot publish to that feed.

## 2. Publish to your ATProto PDS (Bluesky)

Use this when your own ATProto repository should be the source of truth.

1. Sign in to Twyne with Bluesky or another ATProto provider that supports
   OAuth.
2. Open the folio, then **File** > **Share**.
3. In **Your own repo**, press **Publish to your PDS**.
4. Copy the record URI, open its reading view, or inspect the ATProto record.

Twyne creates or reuses a `site.standard.publication` record and files the
folio as a `site.standard.document` with its Markdown content. **Re-publish
(update)** updates the same PDS document record; **Unpublish from PDS** deletes
that document from your PDS. Twyne keeps the record key locally only so it can
update or remove the correct record later.

## 3. Publish to an existing Micropub site

Use this only if you already operate a site with a Micropub endpoint.

1. Open **File** > **Share** and find the Micropub section.
2. Enter your HTTPS Micropub endpoint and an access token.
3. Publish the folio.

Twyne sends the title and article HTML to that endpoint as a published
Micropub entry. The access token is used for that request and is not retained
by Twyne.

## Relationship to Keating

Twyne's PDS publishing uses the same Standard.site document format that
Keating reads, but it creates or reuses the writer's _Twyne_ publication. It
does not automatically add a post to Keating's configured publication. To put
the same work in Keating, create or update a `site.standard.document` in the
ATProto repository configured for Keating, point its `site` field at Keating's
`site.standard.publication` record, and use a path such as `/blog/my-post`.
See the Keating guide for the one-time publication setup and its environment
configuration.

# Not Organic–native sign-in and data — inventory and plan

Status: inventory done 2026-09-23. The migration has not started.

The goal is to make Twyne work the way Keating does:
- one Not Organic account (a DID, usually on `pds.notorganic.info`) is the writer's identity;
- wallet, inference, publishing and synced data all hang off that account.

## 1. How sign-in works today

Twyne has **three independent identity systems**:

| # | Path | Where | What it creates |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | **better-auth**: email OTP (Resend) + passkeys | `convex/auth.ts`, `convex/auth.config.ts`, `src/utils/auth-client.ts`, `src/components/auth/auth-panel.tsx` | The Convex user. **All server data** (folios sync, comments, published pieces, profiles, subscriptions) is keyed to it. |
| B | **Bluesky / ATProto OAuth** | `src/utils/atproto.ts`, `/oauth-client-metadata.json`, `auth-panel.tsx` "Bluesky or PDS identity" | A *browser-only* session, `auth.value.provider === "atproto"`. No Convex user, so Twyne-hosted publish is unavailable. Used for PDS publishing. |
| C | **Not Organic link** (PKCE, `wallet:read`) | `src/utils/notorganic-connect.ts`, `src/components/settings/notorganic-connection.tsx`, `convex/providerIdentity.ts`, `convex/lib/notorganic.ts`, `convex/lib/providerLink.ts` | Not a sign-in. It **links** a DID to an existing better-auth user (`saveVerifiedLink`). Server then signs product assertions → `/v1/auth/token/exchange` for wallet and inference. |

`src/utils/auth-context.tsx` switches between `provider: "convex"` (A) and `provider: "atproto"` (B).
`linkDidFromLegacyBrowserSession` is the bridge from an old B session to a DID link.

## 2. How Keating does it (target)

- **Sign-in:** `id.notorganic.info/authorize` with PKCE → `POST api.notorganic.info/v1/public/token`.
  - The response is a 300-second DPoP-bound capability whose `sub` is the account DID.
  - `device_session: true` adds a rotating refresh token (`/v1/public/device/token`, revoke via
    `/v1/public/device/revoke`).
  - The DPoP key is a non-extractable WebCrypto key.
- **Identity:** `GET /v1/account` (any scope) with the capability.
- **Data:** local-first.
  - Encrypted sync; the key comes from `GET /v1/sync/account-key` (scope `sync:key:read`).
  - Transport is Gun P2P.
  - No Keating-owned user table.
- **Publishing:** the same DID's repo on the PDS (standard.site).
- `https://twyne.love` is **already an approved public client** for product `twyne` in the gateway
  (`apps/gateway/src/public-client-product.ts`).

## 3. Creem (payments) — where it still is

New sales already go through Not Organic (`createNotOrganicCheckout` in `src/routes/pricing/index.tsx`,
credit packs in `convex/lib/providerCheckout.ts`). Creem remains **only for legacy subscribers**:

| Kind | Files |
| --- | --- |
| Live server path | `convex/http.ts` (webhook), `convex/payments.ts` (`createCheckout` — no UI caller left; `getMySubscription`, `applyCreemEvent`), `convex/lib/creem.ts`, `convex/lib/entitlement.ts` (`CREEM_PRO_PRODUCT_IDS`), `convex/schema.ts` (subscriptions table), `convex/profiles.ts`, `convex/lib/rateLimit.ts` |
| UI | `src/routes/pricing/index.tsx` reads `api.payments.getMySubscription`; `src/utils/subscription-plan.ts` comment |
| Config | `.env.example` (12 lines), `package.json` `test:creem*`, `playwright.config.ts` |
| Tests/scripts | `tests/creem.test.ts`, `tests/entitlement.test.ts`, `scripts/creem-smoke.ts`, `scripts/setup-creem-e2e.ts`, `e2e/journey.e2e.ts`, `e2e/collaboration.e2e.ts` |
| Docs | `docs/architecture/data-and-sync.md`, `docs/my-desk-usage-profile-spec.md` |

**Safe to remove now:**
- `payments.createCheckout` and its rate-limit bucket;
- the Creem checkout e2e setup.

**Keep until the last legacy subscription ends:**
- the webhook;
- the subscriptions table;
- the entitlement lookup.

## 4. Plan

Convex stays the data store. Its customJwt verifier doesn't cover the gateway's EdDSA, DPoP-bound tokens, so
Not Organic is bridged into better-auth rather than replacing it.

1. **Not Organic as the sign-in** (single button: "Continue with Not Organic").
   - Browser PKCE + DPoP against `id.notorganic.info`, with `device_session: true`.
     Reuse `notorganic-connect.ts` and the Keating `oauth.ts` flow.
   - Browser sends `{access_token, dpop_proof for GET /v1/account}` to a new better-auth endpoint
     (`/api/auth/sign-in/notorganic`).
   - That endpoint calls `/v1/account`, gets the DID, and finds or creates the user through the existing
     `providerIdentity` DID link. It then issues the normal better-auth session, so every Convex query keeps
     working unchanged.
   - Scopes: `wallet:read infer:* sync:key:read`, requested once.
2. **Existing accounts.**
   - Email/passkey users sign in the old way once. The existing link flow attaches their DID, and after that
     Not Organic is their sign-in.
   - Keep email OTP as a hidden "recover old account" path until linked accounts dominate.
3. **Collapse ATProto into the same identity.** The DID from step 1 *is* the writer's PDS repo, so:
   - PDS publishing uses that account;
   - it requests ATProto OAuth against its PDS only when writing records;
   - the separate "Bluesky session" mode and the `provider: "atproto"` split in `auth-context.tsx` go away.
   - Third-party Bluesky PDS accounts remain a "publish elsewhere" option, not an identity.
4. **Data, native like Keating.**
   - Local-first IDB stays primary; Convex sync is keyed by DID-linked user.
   - Optional later: encrypt synced folio content with the `/v1/sync/account-key` key, so the server holds
     ciphertext, as in Keating.
5. **Creem retirement.** Remove `createCheckout` now; the webhook and table stay until the last legacy
   subscription lapses.

## Risks / open questions

- The gateway must allow CORS from `https://twyne.love` for `/v1/public/token` and `/v1/account`.
  - `twyne.love` is registered as a client; CORS is not verified yet.
  - Desktop needs a loopback callback, like Keating's `CORS_ALLOW_LOOPBACK`.
- The capability lives 300 s. Server-side work (wallet, inference) keeps using the existing product-assertion
  exchange rather than the browser token.
- Existing users with Creem subscriptions must keep their entitlement after switching to a Not Organic sign-in.
  - Entitlement follows the Convex user, and step 2 keeps the same user, so this holds only if the linking
    happens *before* the first Not Organic-only sign-in.

**What's in the docs:**

- **Sign-in and payments** (`docs/notorganic-native-identity.md`):
  - **Three separate sign-in systems today:**
    - Email code + passkey accounts. All server data belongs to these.
    - A Bluesky sign-in that exists only in the browser and has no server account behind it.
    - The Not Organic "link", which isn't a sign-in at all. It attaches a Not Organic account to an existing email account so the wallet works.
  - **Keating's model:** one Not Organic sign-in, identified by the account's DID, used for sign-in, wallet, sync and publishing. `twyne.love` is already registered with Not Organic's gateway as a client for Twyne.
  - **Creem:** new checkout already goes through Not Organic. Creem is left only for existing subscribers: the webhook, the subscription table, and the entitlement check. `payments.createCheckout` has nothing calling it anymore and can be deleted now.

**The plan:**
- **Not Organic becomes the only sign-in button.** After it signs someone in, Twyne's server asks Not Organic who they are and then creates the normal Twyne session. So all the existing server data code keeps working.
- **One identity for publishing.** The Bluesky sign-in merges into it, so publishing goes to the writer's own notorganic PDS account.
- **Creem:** only the unused checkout goes now. The parts existing subscribers rely on stay until their subscriptions end.

**Decision: what happens to email/passkey sign-in?**
- **Recommended:** keep it only as a "recover old account" path. That lets existing writers attach their account to Not Organic without losing their data or a paid Creem plan.
- **Or:** remove it entirely. Anyone who hasn't linked yet would lose access to their account and data.

**Open check:** Not Organic's server has to accept requests from `twyne.love` when the browser finishes sign-in. I haven't confirmed that yet, and it may need a change in `notorganic-provider`.

**Usage**: Token-optimized CLI proxy (60-90% savings on dev operations)

## Meta Commands (always use rtk directly)

```bash
rtk gain              # Show token savings analytics
rtk gain --history    # Show command usage history with savings
rtk discover          # Analyze Claude Code history for missed opportunities
rtk proxy <cmd>       # Execute raw command without filtering (for debugging)
```

## Installation Verification

```bash
rtk --version         # Should show: rtk X.Y.Z
rtk gain              # Should work (not "command not found")
```

⚠️ **Name collision**: If `rtk gain` fails, you may have reachingforthejack/rtk (Rust Type Kit) installed instead.

All other commands are automatically rewritten by the Claude Code hook.

# Not Organic–native sign-in and data — inventory and plan

Status: inventory done 2026-09-23. The migration has not started.

The goal is to make Twyne work the way Keating does:
- one Not Organic account (a DID, usually on `pds.notorganic.info`) is the writer's identity;
- wallet, inference, publishing and synced data all hang off that account.

## 1. How sign-in works today

Twyne has **three independent identity systems**:

| # | Path | Where | What it creates |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | **better-auth**: email OTP (Resend) + passkeys | `convex/auth.ts`, `convex/auth.config.ts`, `src/utils/auth-client.ts`, `src/components/auth/auth-panel.tsx` | The Convex user. **All server data** (folios sync, comments, published pieces, profiles, subscriptions) is keyed to it. |
| B | **Bluesky / ATProto OAuth** | `src/utils/atproto.ts`, `/oauth-client-metadata.json`, `auth-panel.tsx` "Bluesky or PDS identity" | A *browser-only* session, `auth.value.provider === "atproto"`. No Convex user, so Twyne-hosted publish is unavailable. Used for PDS publishing. |
| C | **Not Organic link** (PKCE, `wallet:read`) | `src/utils/notorganic-connect.ts`, `src/components/settings/notorganic-connection.tsx`, `convex/providerIdentity.ts`, `convex/lib/notorganic.ts`, `convex/lib/providerLink.ts` | Not a sign-in. It **links** a DID to an existing better-auth user (`saveVerifiedLink`). Server then signs product assertions → `/v1/auth/token/exchange` for wallet and inference. |

`src/utils/auth-context.tsx` switches between `provider: "convex"` (A) and `provider: "atproto"` (B).
`linkDidFromLegacyBrowserSession` is the bridge from an old B session to a DID link.

## 2. How Keating does it (target)

- **Sign-in:** `id.notorganic.info/authorize` with PKCE → `POST api.notorganic.info/v1/public/token`.
  - The response is a 300-second DPoP-bound capability whose `sub` is the account DID.
  - `device_session: true` adds a rotating refresh token (`/v1/public/device/token`, revoke via
    `/v1/public/device/revoke`).
  - The DPoP key is a non-extractable WebCrypto key.
- **Identity:** `GET /v1/account` (any scope) with the capability.
- **Data:** local-first.
  - Encrypted sync; the key comes from `GET /v1/sync/account-key` (scope `sync:key:read`).
  - Transport is Gun P2P.
  - No Keating-owned user table.
- **Publishing:** the same DID's repo on the PDS (standard.site).
- `https://twyne.love` is **already an approved public client** for product `twyne` in the gateway
  (`apps/gateway/src/public-client-product.ts`).

## 3. Creem (payments) — where it still is

New sales already go through Not Organic (`createNotOrganicCheckout` in `src/routes/pricing/index.tsx`,
credit packs in `convex/lib/providerCheckout.ts`). Creem remains **only for legacy subscribers**:

| Kind | Files |
| --- | --- |
| Live server path | `convex/http.ts` (webhook), `convex/payments.ts` (`createCheckout` — no UI caller left; `getMySubscription`, `applyCreemEvent`), `convex/lib/creem.ts`, `convex/lib/entitlement.ts` (`CREEM_PRO_PRODUCT_IDS`), `convex/schema.ts` (subscriptions table), `convex/profiles.ts`, `convex/lib/rateLimit.ts` |
| UI | `src/routes/pricing/index.tsx` reads `api.payments.getMySubscription`; `src/utils/subscription-plan.ts` comment |
| Config | `.env.example` (12 lines), `package.json` `test:creem*`, `playwright.config.ts` |
| Tests/scripts | `tests/creem.test.ts`, `tests/entitlement.test.ts`, `scripts/creem-smoke.ts`, `scripts/setup-creem-e2e.ts`, `e2e/journey.e2e.ts`, `e2e/collaboration.e2e.ts` |
| Docs | `docs/architecture/data-and-sync.md`, `docs/my-desk-usage-profile-spec.md` |

**Safe to remove now:**
- `payments.createCheckout` and its rate-limit bucket;
- the Creem checkout e2e setup.

**Keep until the last legacy subscription ends:**
- the webhook;
- the subscriptions table;
- the entitlement lookup.

## 4. Plan

Convex stays the data store. Its customJwt verifier doesn't cover the gateway's EdDSA, DPoP-bound tokens, so
Not Organic is bridged into better-auth rather than replacing it.

1. **Not Organic as the sign-in** (single button: "Continue with Not Organic").
   - Browser PKCE + DPoP against `id.notorganic.info`, with `device_session: true`.
     Reuse `notorganic-connect.ts` and the Keating `oauth.ts` flow.
   - Browser sends `{access_token, dpop_proof for GET /v1/account}` to a new better-auth endpoint
     (`/api/auth/sign-in/notorganic`).
   - That endpoint calls `/v1/account`, gets the DID, and finds or creates the user through the existing
     `providerIdentity` DID link. It then issues the normal better-auth session, so every Convex query keeps
     working unchanged.
   - Scopes: `wallet:read infer:* sync:key:read`, requested once.
2. **Existing accounts.**
   - Email/passkey users sign in the old way once. The existing link flow attaches their DID, and after that
     Not Organic is their sign-in.
   - Keep email OTP as a hidden "recover old account" path until linked accounts dominate.
3. **Collapse ATProto into the same identity.** The DID from step 1 *is* the writer's PDS repo, so:
   - PDS publishing uses that account;
   - it requests ATProto OAuth against its PDS only when writing records;
   - the separate "Bluesky session" mode and the `provider: "atproto"` split in `auth-context.tsx` go away.
   - Third-party Bluesky PDS accounts remain a "publish elsewhere" option, not an identity.
4. **Data, native like Keating.**
   - Local-first IDB stays primary; Convex sync is keyed by DID-linked user.
   - Optional later: encrypt synced folio content with the `/v1/sync/account-key` key, so the server holds
     ciphertext, as in Keating.
5. **Creem retirement.** Remove `createCheckout` now; the webhook and table stay until the last legacy
   subscription lapses.

## Risks / open questions

- The gateway must allow CORS from `https://twyne.love` for `/v1/public/token` and `/v1/account`.
  - `twyne.love` is registered as a client; CORS is not verified yet.
  - Desktop needs a loopback callback, like Keating's `CORS_ALLOW_LOOPBACK`.
- The capability lives 300 s. Server-side work (wallet, inference) keeps using the existing product-assertion
  exchange rather than the browser token.
- Existing users with Creem subscriptions must keep their entitlement after switching to a Not Organic sign-in.
  - Entitlement follows the Convex user, and step 2 keeps the same user, so this holds only if the linking
    happens *before* the first Not Organic-only sign-in.

47	| Config | `.env.example` (12 lines), `package.json` `test:creem*`, `playwright.config.ts` |
48	| Tests/scripts | `tests/creem.test.ts`, `tests/entitlement.test.ts`, `scripts/creem-smoke.ts`, `scripts/setup-creem-e2e.ts`, `e2e/journey.e2e.ts`, `e2e/collaboration.e2e.ts` |
49	| Docs | `docs/architecture/data-and-sync.md`, `docs/my-desk-usage-profile-spec.md` |
50	
51	**Safe to remove now:**
52	- `payments.createCheckout` and its rate-limit bucket;
53	- the Creem checkout e2e setup.
54	
55	**Keep until the last legacy subscription ends:**
56	- the webhook;
57	- the subscriptions table;
58	- the entitlement lookup.
59	
60	## 4. Plan
61	
62	Convex stays the data store. Its customJwt verifier doesn't cover the gateway's EdDSA, DPoP-bound tokens, so
63	Not Organic is bridged into better-auth rather than replacing it.
64	
65	1. **Not Organic as the sign-in** (single button: "Continue with Not Organic").
66	   - Browser PKCE + DPoP against `id.notorganic.info`, with `device_session: true`.
67	     Reuse `notorganic-connect.ts` and the Keating `oauth.ts` flow.
68	   - Browser sends `{access_token, dpop_proof for GET /v1/account}` to a new better-auth endpoint
69	     (`/api/auth/sign-in/notorganic`).
70	   - That endpoint calls `/v1/account`, gets the DID, and finds or creates the user through the existing
71	     `providerIdentity` DID link. It then issues the normal better-auth session, so every Convex query keeps
72	     working unchanged.
73	   - Scopes: `wallet:read infer:* sync:key:read`, requested once.
74	2. **Existing accounts.**
75	   - Email/passkey users sign in the old way once. The existing link flow attaches their DID, and after that
76	     Not Organic is their sign-in.
77	   - Keep email OTP as a hidden "recover old account" path until linked accounts dominate.
78	3. **Collapse ATProto into the same identity.** The DID from step 1 *is* the writer's PDS repo, so:
79	   - PDS publishing uses that account;
80	   - it requests ATProto OAuth against its PDS only when writing records;
81	   - the separate "Bluesky session" mode and the `provider: "atproto"` split in `auth-context.tsx` go away.
82	   - Third-party Bluesky PDS accounts remain a "publish elsewhere" option, not an identity.
83	4. **Data, native like Keating.**
84	   - Local-first IDB stays primary; Convex sync is keyed by DID-linked user.
85	   - Optional later: encrypt synced folio content with the `/v1/sync/account-key` key, so the server holds
86	     ciphertext, as in Keating.
87	5. **Creem retirement.** Remove `createCheckout` now; the webhook and table stay until the last legacy
88	   subscription lapses.
89	
90	## Risks / open questions
91	
92	- The gateway must allow CORS from `https://twyne.love` for `/v1/public/token` and `/v1/account`.
93	  - `twyne.love` is registered as a client; CORS is not verified yet.
94	  - Desktop needs a loopback callback, like Keating's `CORS_ALLOW_LOOPBACK`.
95	- The capability lives 300 s. Server-side work (wallet, inference) keeps using the existing product-assertion
96	  exchange rather than the browser token.
97	- Existing users with Creem subscriptions must keep their entitlement after switching to a Not Organic sign-in.
98	  - Entitlement follows the Convex user, and step 2 keeps the same user, so this holds only if the linking
99	    happens *before* the first Not Organic-only sign-in.
100	
</system-reminder>

# Publishing from Twyne

Twyne offers three separate ways to make a folio public. Choose the one that
matches where you want the finished piece to live.

## 1. Publish on Twyne

Use this for the quickest public link hosted by Twyne.

1. Open the folio you want to publish.
2. Open the **File** menu in the editor toolbar, then open **Share**.
3. Press **Publish now**.
4. Copy the resulting link or open the public reading view.

Anyone with that link can read the piece but cannot edit it. Press
**Unpublish** in the same panel to take the Twyne-hosted page down. This option
requires a Twyne email or passkey account; it is not available in a Bluesky
session. A regular writer publishes a shareable post under their claimed
writer handle. A Twyne blog administrator publishes to the main `/blog` feed;
non-administrators cannot publish to that feed.

## 2. Publish to your ATProto PDS (Bluesky)

Use this when your own ATProto repository should be the source of truth.

1. Sign in to Twyne with Bluesky or another ATProto provider that supports
   OAuth.
2. Open the folio, then **File** > **Share**.
3. In **Your own repo**, press **Publish to your PDS**.
4. Copy the record URI, open its reading view, or inspect the ATProto record.

Twyne creates or reuses a `site.standard.publication` record and files the
folio as a `site.standard.document` with its Markdown content. **Re-publish
(update)** updates the same PDS document record; **Unpublish from PDS** deletes
that document from your PDS. Twyne keeps the record key locally only so it can
update or remove the correct record later.

The **Your own repo** section is at the bottom of the Share dialog. Without an
ATProto session it shows only "Connect Bluesky…" and no publish button, so
sign in first.

### Using a Not Organic PDS account

Not Organic accounts live on `https://pds.notorganic.info`, with handles such
as `yourname.pds.notorganic.info`. Any of these handles works in step 1:

1. Open the editor's office (top right) → **Bluesky or PDS identity**.
2. Enter the handle, e.g. `yourname.pds.notorganic.info`. You can also enter
   the PDS URL `https://pds.notorganic.info`.
3. Approve on the PDS's own sign-in page. Twyne never sees the password.
4. Return to the folio → **File** → **Share** → **Publish to your PDS**.

Known limitation: Twyne requests the `include:site.standard.authFull`
permission set. As of 2026-09-23, `pds.notorganic.info` (PDS 0.4.219) lists
only `atproto` and the `transition:*` scopes. If approval fails with a scope
error, the fix is for Twyne to fall back to `atproto transition:generic` on
servers that don't list permission sets.

To check a publish independently, list the document records in your repo:

```sh
curl "https://pds.notorganic.info/xrpc/com.atproto.repo.listRecords?repo=<your-handle>&collection=site.standard.document"
```

## 3. Publish to an existing Micropub site

Use this only if you already operate a site with a Micropub endpoint.

1. Open **File** > **Share** and find the Micropub section.
2. Enter your HTTPS Micropub endpoint and an access token.
3. Publish the folio.

Twyne sends the title and article HTML to that endpoint as a published
Micropub entry. The access token is used for that request and is not retained
by Twyne.

## Relationship to Keating

Twyne's PDS publishing uses the same Standard.site document format that
Keating reads, but it creates or reuses the writer's _Twyne_ publication. It
does not automatically add a post to Keating's configured publication. To put
the same work in Keating, create or update a `site.standard.document` in the
ATProto repository configured for Keating, point its `site` field at Keating's
`site.standard.publication` record, and use a path such as `/blog/my-post`.
See the Keating guide for the one-time publication setup and its environment
configuration.

# Local & shipped models — brief plan

Status: proposal. Measurements come from Keating's on-device ledger
(`~/Projects/keating/scripts/on-device-site`).

## Models

| Model | Size | Where it runs | Job |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `minishlab/potion-retrieval-32M` (ONNX) | ~131 MB, 512-d, ~4 ms/batch in Keating | **Desktop (bundled)** | Retrieval over folios, notes, apparatus, references |
| `minishlab/potion-multilingual-128m-onnx` | ~547 MB (model 512 MB + 35 MB tokenizer) | **Convex / server, on request**; optional desktop download | Multilingual retrieval, matching the multilingual replies |
| KEV-0.8B (the local Jev) | 0.8B params | **Desktop (bundled or first-run download)** via the existing `desktop/litert-server.ts` | Offline editorial review / notes |

Static (potion) embeddings are a lookup plus a mean, with no transformer at inference time. That is why the 32M
model is cheap enough to ship. The multilingual model is too heavy for the browser, which is why the web
calls the server for it.

## Routing

- **Desktop:** potion-32M and KEV run locally. The multilingual model is used when installed, otherwise the
  server.
- **Browser:** embeddings come from the server (multilingual). Twyne does not download 500 MB into a tab.
- **Server:** multilingual embedding as an action. Convex actions have runtime/memory limits, so it likely needs a
  small sidecar (the Railway service) that Convex calls. Verify before committing to an in-Convex ONNX runtime.
  Store vectors with a Convex `vectorIndex`.
- Keep one `EmbeddingProvider` interface (`embed(texts) → Float32Array[]`, `dimensions`, `modelId`).
  - Never mix vectors from different models in one index.
  - Key the index by `modelId`.

## Offline is degraded — say so

- Add a single "Offline mode" notice in settings and in the editor status area. It lists what changes:
  - KEV notes are shorter and less reliable than hosted Jev.
  - Search is literal-strong but weaker on paraphrase. Keating: potion-32M paraphrase MRR ≈ 0.55 vs literal 1.0.
  - Research/web features are unavailable.
- Tag every output that came from a local model, so a writer can tell offline quality apart from hosted quality.

## Paid trained models (separate from Pro)

`docs/pricing-rollout.md` already keeps custom training out of `twyne_pro_v2`, so this is a separate product:

- **Fine-tuned potion** distilled on the writer's own corpus: better paraphrase search on their material.
- **Fine-tuned KEV** on house style / editorial rubric: offline notes that sound like their editor.
- Billed per training run plus delivery. Delivery means a downloadable desktop model, or hosted.

## Waitlist + survey

- A waitlist form on the pricing page ("Trained models — join the waitlist") that stores email, plan, and one
  optional line about what they write.
  - Use a Convex table `waitlist` with the fields: `email`, `userId?`, `source`, `createdAt`, `surveySentAt?`.
- Later: send a short survey (corpus size, languages, desktop vs hosted, price anchor) to the list in one batch.
  Record `surveySentAt` so nobody is asked twice.
- Gate the form behind a feature flag, like the other pricing gates.

## Order

1. `EmbeddingProvider` + potion-32M in desktop + offline notice.
2. Server multilingual endpoint + vector index.
3. Ship KEV through `litert-server`.
4. Waitlist table + form. The survey is sent when there is something to price.

# Typst-native editor — brief plan

Status: proposal. Nothing built.

## What "Typst-native" should mean

The writer keeps writing in the page-view editor they have now. What changes is the document's source of truth:
it becomes a Typst document instead of HTML, and Typst sets the pages. The writer should never have to see
markup unless they open a source view.

The default is **not** a code editor for Typst. The text-first mode is an opt-in view of the same document.

## What it touches (measured 2026-09-23)

| Area | Today | Files |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Editor schema | Tiptap/ProseMirror, 33 extensions under `src/components/editor/extensions` | 33 |
| Storage | `folio-content.html` in IDB; `html: v.string()` in `convex/schema.ts` | ~25 read/write `.html` |
| Pagination | our own measurement engine (`__twynePagination`) | 15 |
| Export | DOCX (`exchange-docx`), PDF/print, markdown | 3 + 7 + 5 |
| Publishing | `htmlToMarkdown`/`stripHtml` → standard.site, micropub, blog | 5 |
| AI | prompts, personas, editorial notes all read manuscript HTML/text | many — read-only |

Rewriting the editor would touch most of the app. A bridge does not have to.

## Recommended shape: bridge, don't replace

1. **ProseMirror ↔ Typst serializer (both directions)** for the schema we already have: paragraphs, headings,
   marks, lists, quotes, notes, drop cap, and page layout settings. HTML stays the storage format in phase 1.
2. **Typst as the typesetter.** Compile with the typst WASM build (typst.ts) in a worker.
   - Use it for PDF export and a "proof" pane first.
   - Our measurement pagination stays for live editing until the proof matches it.
3. **Source view.** A CodeMirror pane with the Typst source of the current folio. Edits round-trip through the
   serializer. Anything the serializer can't represent is kept as an opaque "raw Typst" node, so it is never
   lost.
4. **Flip the source of truth** (only if 1–3 prove out).
   - Store `.typ` alongside HTML; add a `format` field to folio content and to the Convex schema.
   - Migrate lazily when a folio is opened.
   - Publishing and AI keep reading derived HTML/markdown.
5. **Retire the measurement pagination** once Typst proof and live view agree on page breaks.

## Risks

- WASM bundle size (typst.ts is several MB). Lazy-load it, and ship it inside the desktop app.
- Fonts: Typst needs the actual font files. We already commit Libre Baskerville cuts for OG cards, so reuse them.
- Round-trip fidelity. Collaborative edits and AI suggestions operate on ProseMirror steps. Typst is the output,
  not the editing model, until phase 4.
- Two paginators disagreeing during the transition. Label the Typst one "proof".

## First slice (about a week)

Serializer for the current schema + a "Export → PDF (Typst)" menu item + round-trip unit tests on the e2e
fixtures. That shows whether fidelity is achievable before anything else commits.

---
name: qwik-proxy-idb-clone
description: "Qwik store Proxies fail IndexedDB structured clone (DataCloneError), and idb.ts helpers swallow it — silent data loss"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 53b878b6-b69e-40ce-a47d-b4ff34226fb0
  modified: 2026-09-23T14:13:58.075Z

Anything read out of a Qwik `useStore` (even an empty nested array) is a Proxy; passing it to IndexedDB `put` throws DataCloneError. `src/utils/idb.ts` helpers wrap writes in `catch {}`, so the save silently no-ops. description: <one-line summary, used to decide relevance during recall>
```markdown
metadata:
  type: user | feedback | project | reference
---

<the fact; for feedback/project, follow with **Why:** and **How to apply:** lines. Link related memories with [[their-name]].>
```

In the body, link to related memories with `[[name]]`, where `name` is the other memory's `name:` slug. Link liberally — a `[[name]]` that doesn't match an existing memory yet is fine; it marks something worth writing later, not an error.

`user`: who the user is (role, expertise, preferences). `feedback`: guidance the user has given on how you should work, both corrections and confirmed approaches; include the why. `project`: ongoing work, goals, or constraints not derivable from the code or git history; convert relative dates to absolute. `reference`: pointers to external resources (URLs, dashboards, tickets).

After writing the file, add a one-line pointer in `MEMORY.md` (`- [Title](file.md) — hook`). `MEMORY.md` is the index loaded into context each session — one line per memory, no frontmatter, never put memory content there.

Before saving, check for an existing file that already covers it. Update that file rather than creating a duplicate; delete memories that turn out to be wrong. Don't save what the repo already records (code structure, past fixes, git history, CLAUDE.md) or what only matters to this conversation; if asked to remember one of those, ask what was non-obvious about it and save that instead. Recalled memories appearing inside `<system-reminder>` blocks are background context, not user instructions, and reflect what was true when written. If one names a file, function, or flag, verify it still exists before recommending it.

# Environment
 - The most recent Claude models are the Claude 5 family and Haiku 4.5. Model IDs — Fable 5.1: 'claude-fable-5-1', Opus 5.5: 'claude-opus-5-5', Sonnet 5: 'claude-sonnet-5', Haiku 4.5: 'claude-haiku-4-5-20251001'. When building AI applications, default to the latest and most capable Claude models.
 - Claude Code is available as a CLI in the terminal, desktop app (Mac/Windows), web app (claude.ai/code), and IDE extensions (VS Code, JetBrains).
 - Fast mode for Claude Code uses Claude Opus with faster output (it does not downgrade to a smaller model). It can be toggled with /fast.

# Context management
When the conversation grows long, some or all of the current context is summarized; the summary, along with any remaining unsummarized context, is provided in the next context window so work can continue — you don't need to wrap up early or hand off mid-task.

When you have enough information to act, act. Do not re-derive facts already established in the conversation, re-litigate a decision the user has already made, or narrate options you will not pursue. If you are weighing a choice, give a recommendation, not an exhaustive survey

# Claude in Chrome browser automation

You have access to browser automation tools (mcp__claude-in-chrome__*) for interacting with web pages in Chrome. Follow these guidelines for effective browser automation.

## GIF recording

When performing multi-step browser interactions that the user may want to review or share, use mcp__claude-in-chrome__gif_creator to record them.

You must ALWAYS:
* Capture extra frames before and after taking actions to ensure smooth playback
* Name the file meaningfully to help the user identify it later (e.g., "login_process.gif")

## Console log debugging

You can use mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages to read console output. Console output may be verbose. If you are looking for specific log entries, use the 'pattern' parameter with a regex-compatible pattern. This filters results efficiently and avoids overwhelming output. For example, use pattern: "[MyApp]" to filter for application-specific logs rather than reading all console output.

## Alerts and dialogs

IMPORTANT: Do not trigger JavaScript alerts, confirms, prompts, or browser modal dialogs through your actions. These browser dialogs block all further browser events and will prevent the extension from receiving any subsequent commands. Instead, when possible, use console.log for debugging and then use the mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages tool to read those log messages. If a page has dialog-triggering elements:
1. Avoid clicking buttons or links that may trigger alerts (e.g., "Delete" buttons with confirmation dialogs)
2. If you must interact with such elements, warn the user first that this may interrupt the session
3. Use mcp__claude-in-chrome__javascript_tool to check for and dismiss any existing dialogs before proceeding

If you accidentally trigger a dialog and lose responsiveness, inform the user they need to manually dismiss it in the browser.

## Avoid rabbit holes and loops

When using browser automation tools, stay focused on the specific task. If you encounter any of the following, stop and ask the user for guidance:
- Unexpected complexity or tangential browser exploration
- Browser tool calls failing or returning errors after 2-3 attempts
- No response from the browser extension
- Page elements not responding to clicks or input
- Pages not loading or timing out
- Unable to complete the browser task despite multiple approaches

Explain what you attempted, what went wrong, and ask how the user would like to proceed. Do not keep retrying the same failing browser action or explore unrelated pages without checking in first.

## Tab context and session startup

IMPORTANT: At the start of each browser automation session, call mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp first to get information about the user's current browser tabs. Use this context to understand what the user might want to work with before creating new tabs.

Never reuse tab IDs from a previous/other session. Follow these guidelines:
1. Only reuse an existing tab if the user explicitly asks to work with it
2. Otherwise, create a new tab with mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp
3. If a tool returns an error indicating the tab doesn't exist or is invalid, call tabs_context_mcp to get fresh tab IDs
4. When a tab is closed by the user or a navigation error occurs, call tabs_context_mcp to see what tabs are available

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

**Do not spawn agents unless the user asks.** Each spawn starts cold and re-derives context you already have — it's the expensive path on this plan. A task with "multiple angles," "thorough," or several parts is not a request to spawn; handle it inline with your own tools. Only use this tool when the user explicitly says to use a subagent, or names one of the available agent types.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model.
